_readme: Blueprints for the Hub's shared UI layer. This file is the AUTHORED half of the
catalog; the CSS half is read live off static/css/base.css + chrome.css + the
stylesheets static/js/theme-switch.js injects at runtime, by extract.py, and is
deliberately NOT stored here (copied CSS goes stale in silence).
tier        = which /blueprints tab the entry sits on: basics (type, colour,
small controls and titles), elements (cards, tabs, tables: parts
a page composes) or modules (prebuilt chrome that mounts whole).
Full pages are the origins list, the fourth tab.
classes     = namespaced roots this component owns. Matched as bare class names
by the override check, so ONLY put unambiguous names here.
descendants = full selectors for generically-named children (.ok, .dim, .sep,
.meta, .kbd ...). Display and coverage only, never matched bare -
.save-status.ok in batch has nothing to do with the status strip,
and keying on the bare word produced 11 false positives.
signature   = OPTIONAL regexes over declarations that ARE this component. A module
rule reproducing one is a copy. Ceiling: catches copy-paste-then-drift
(the failure that actually happened), NOT a from-scratch reinvention
using different properties. Nothing static can catch that.
live        = CSS selector for a REAL instance of the component on the running
/blueprints page. The page clones that node for the preview and derives
the paste-able markup from its outerHTML, so the markup cannot be
wrong -- it IS the shipped DOM. Every chrome component is drawn by
topbar.jsx at runtime and exists in no template, which is why
hand-authored markup for them was invented and every field was wrong
(a made-up brand-mark path, a made-up surface glyph, a made-up
command-K hint, launcher tiles with no glyphs). Prefer live.
`open` first clicks the modules button, for the overlay.
markup      = what a PAGE AUTHOR actually types. For the chrome components that is
only the extras-only shell (topbar.jsx fills it), and for the four it
mounts from nothing it is the empty string -- you write no markup at
all. Never invented: every non-empty value is transcribed verbatim
from the real file named in markup_from. Check 5 asserts its classes
are all claimed by this entry, and for an entry with no `live` that
the two sets match exactly, so an invented or incomplete field fails.
exactly, in both directions, so an invented or incomplete field fails.
Adding a shared class without a blueprint fails the suite. That is the point.
origins     = top-level list, one entry per layout origin (base a dashboard is
built from). skeleton/skeleton_from, composes, theme_hooks and
signature are origin-only fields; classes/descendants/template_classes
work the same as a component blueprint's. See docs/specs/
2026-09-17-layout-blueprints-origin-derivative-design.md.
derivatives = top-level list, one entry per dashboard built on an origin. `origin`
names the origins[].id it links; `template` and `page_mods` are the
dashboard's own files (page_mods must be in baselines.page_css_files);
`body_class` is the class the derivative's <body> carries; `href` is
where the layouts tab links it. Edits are file edits -- register a
new derivative here after pasting the origin's skeleton, never before.

blueprints.name: Top bar
blueprints.purpose: The global page header: the back control and brand lockup on the left, the page crumb beside it, and the right-hand control cluster.
blueprints.use_when: Every Hub page. It is chrome, not a per-page header. Ship <header class="topbar"> holding only the page's own extras, each tagged data-slot: crumb (the page title, a pill, a section line), lead (between brand and crumb), left (after the crumb block), right (ahead of the controls; untagged lands here). topbar.jsx draws back, brand, toggle, theme picker, sign-out and modules around them and moves the extras in, so their ids and listeners survive. The page loads react + react-dom and /jsx/static/js/topbar.jsx after theme-switch.js. React pages render <Topbar crumb="..."/>.
blueprints.dont: Never re-declare .topbar in a module stylesheet to change its height or padding. It is 56px because the bar is chrome; four modules already override it and that is the drift this catalog exists to stop. Do not write the brand, back, toggle, picker or modules button into the HTML either -- the slogan is theme-flavoured and topbar.jsx draws it from HubTheme.slogan(). .brand-mark and .crumb-meta are declared but NO page renders either; treat them as unused, not as components to reach for.

blueprints.name: Back button
blueprints.purpose: The universal back control -- first thing in the left cluster, on every page except home.
blueprints.use_when: Nowhere by hand. topbar.jsx draws it on every page that is not home; it needs no markup and no anchor.
blueprints.dont: Do not add a per-module back link. Do not size it or box it like the other controls: it is the bar's full-height edge tab (align-self:stretch, fixed 44px wide), the one control that deliberately does not take --ctl-h.

blueprints.name: Surface toggle
blueprints.purpose: The light/dark switch in the top bar's right cluster. Renders as a moon or sun glyph, never a word.
blueprints.use_when: Nowhere by hand. topbar.jsx draws it (id surfaceToggle) and HubTheme.surface in theme-switch.js persists the choice.
blueprints.dont: Do not build a second light/dark control, and do not write the glyph yourself. The surface axis is global and persisted in localStorage; a page-local toggle desynchronises from every other page. Writing the word "dark"/"light" here is the specific drift test_topbar_parity.py exists to catch -- it recurred about seven times.

blueprints.name: Control pane
blueprints.purpose: The gear in every bar that opens one panel: light/dark, theme, liquid's transparency and sign out (Workbench pick 2026-10-17). The older .theme-picker-* classes stay as the dropdown dress other pickers reuse (trips account).
blueprints.use_when: Nowhere by hand. topbar.jsx draws it in every bar, and into [data-theme-picker] where a page has no bar (login).
blueprints.dont: Do not add a theme control of your own and do not write theme names into a page. The theme list is theme-switch.js's (HubTheme.list); a hard-coded copy goes stale the moment a theme is added or retired.

blueprints.name: Launcher button
blueprints.purpose: The top-bar control that opens the module launcher. Rightmost in the cluster, on every page.
blueprints.use_when: Nowhere by hand. topbar.jsx draws it from window.MODULES, so the page's only job is to load /hub-modules.js. Miss that and there is no modules button at all.
blueprints.dont: Do not give it a keyboard hint. topbar.jsx renders a plain modules and stays that way. Do not restyle it per module -- it is the same affordance everywhere by design.

blueprints.name: Notification bell
blueprints.purpose: The bell in the top bar: an unread count badge and a glass drop-down listing new above earlier notifications, each row led by its module's launcher icon in a glass tile.
blueprints.use_when: Nowhere by hand. topbar.jsx draws it before the control pane on every page that loads /hub-modules.js. A module posts with notify.post(...) from Python; it never touches the bar.
blueprints.dont: Do not render a notification title or body as HTML, and do not draw a second bell or badge per module. The bar must keep working when the store fails, so the bell fails quiet.

blueprints.name: Module launcher
blueprints.purpose: The full-screen overlay listing every Hub module, tiered home / workspaces / utilities. Each tile carries an inline SVG glyph.
blueprints.use_when: Opened from the launcher button on any page. Reuse the tile markup if you need a grid of destinations.
blueprints.dont: Do not copy .launch-tile's hover treatment into a module grid; scope to the shared class instead, the way work.css does with .work-grid .launch-tile. Do not give .launch-panel its own max-height rule -- it already handles short windows and phones in landscape. Do not hand-write a tile: the glyph is an inline SVG that hub_modules.py owns.

blueprints.name: Status strip
blueprints.purpose: The footer strip on every page, one component like the top bar (StatusStrip in topbar.jsx): clock, ambient date, the page's own context, connector dots where the page loaded them, build tag.
blueprints.use_when: Every page with a bottom bar. React pages render <StatusStrip> with their context as children; plain pages ship a <footer class="status"> holding only their context and topbar.jsx moves those nodes into the strip, so ids a page script writes keep working.
blueprints.dont: Do not hand-write the clock or date, and do not re-declare .status in a module stylesheet: the base lives in base.css and the liquid island in liquid.css. Because .status shares a grid column with the top bar and the page body, a width change there stretches the whole shell past the viewport (the /work clipping bug).

blueprints.name: Modal
blueprints.purpose: Themed replacement for the native alert / confirm / prompt dialogs.
blueprints.use_when: Any confirm, message box, or small form. It mirrors the launcher's scrim idiom with the same tokens. Ship the empty scrim in the page and fill .hub-modal at call time.
blueprints.dont: Never call window.confirm or window.alert. Never restyle the scrim per module. The scrim ships with [hidden] and an explicit [hidden]{display:none} override, because an author display:flex beats the UA rule at equal specificity; toggle with el.hidden, not style.display.

blueprints.name: Modal, form variants
blueprints.purpose: The three parts a form dialog needs that a confirm dialog does not: a wider frame, a two-column field grid, and a line of context under the title.
blueprints.use_when: A dialog that collects more than a couple of fields. Put --wide on the .hub-modal itself and only when the field count earns it; a one-field dialog stays the width of its one field. The grid goes on a wrapper inside the body, and a field that needs the full width opts out in the module's own sheet.
blueprints.dont: Never restate the dialog itself beside these. That is what trips did until 2026-09-16: a second .modal that had drifted to a 460px width, a --line-strong border and no scrim blur, sitting next to the shared one it was a copy of, and the copy check never saw it because the values no longer matched.
blueprints.why: A form dialog and a confirm dialog are the same dialog with a different payload, so the frame stays in base.css and only the payload's needs land here. Splitting them the other way, a separate form-dialog component, is what produced the drifted copy in the first place.

blueprints.name: Inline error
blueprints.purpose: The visible failure state for a fetch that would otherwise fail silently.
blueprints.use_when: Every fetch that can fail. A panel that renders empty on error is indistinguishable from one with no data.
blueprints.dont: Do not swallow a failed fetch. Do not invent a per-module error style. Append the block as a CHILD rather than overwriting the container's className -- several containers carry a layout class that has to survive the next successful render.

blueprints.name: Status dot
blueprints.purpose: A small coloured dot preceding a text label. Caller sets --dot-color.
blueprints.use_when: Beside a state label. The dot is the decoration; the text carries the state.
blueprints.dont: Never use the dot alone as the state indicator. Colour on its own conveys nothing to a colourblind or screen-reader user, which is why the CSS comment demands a paired label.

blueprints.name: Button
blueprints.purpose: The Hub's outline button. A 1px border, a muted label, and a hover that borrows the accent; --lg is the same button at 14px with a glyph slot beside the label.
blueprints.use_when: Any action that is not the dialog's own cancel/save pair, which base.css owns as hub-modal-btn. --danger for a delete, --accent for the one action in a row worth pointing at, --lg where the buttons sit in a 14px column rather than a dense list.
blueprints.dont: Do not define a bare .btn in a module sheet. Three modules each did, and because a module sheet loads before components.css a module modifier at equal specificity now loses to the promoted base: write it .hub-btn.<modifier> instead, the way jobs' fill-on-hover tones are.
blueprints.why: Trips' and jobs' hover rule was byte-identical and their base differed only in size, which is what a modifier is for. Nothing a button paints is a fact about a trip or a job application; the label is the only part that knows what it does.

blueprints.name: Tabs
blueprints.purpose: A strip of tabs over a 1px rule, each one carrying a 2px underline that stays transparent until it is the tab you are on. --segmented is the same control drawn as filled pills inside a bordered track.
blueprints.use_when: A choice between sibling views of the same page. Plain for a section switch, --segmented for a choice of MODE where the options are a short closed set and the control should read as one object. The active declaration is yours: set the underline colour, and the label colour if the page wants the live tab louder.
blueprints.dont: Do not restate the underline. Six modules each wrote `border-bottom: 2px solid transparent` with a `-1px` pull beside it, which is the whole affordance. Do not reach for --segmented for a pill strip that has no track: juniper & co's sub-tabs fill in foreground on an elevated bar and are deliberately a different control from the tabs above them.
blueprints.why: Nothing a tab paints is a fact about its page. The strip, the transparent underline and the -1px pull that lands it on the rule are the same in every module that has tabs; what differed was type and how loud the live tab reads, and both of those are one declaration in the module's own sheet.

blueprints.name: Numeric cell
blueprints.purpose: A table cell holding a figure. Right-aligned so the values line up against each other, tabular lining figures so the digits line up down the column.
blueprints.use_when: Any th or td whose content is a number: money, a count, a percentage, a rate. Put it on the header as well as the cells, so the heading sits over the figures rather than beside them.
blueprints.dont: Do not set the face here. Trips reads its money in the display serif and finances reads its in the body face, and that is a page's own reading. Do not expect this to win against a th or td rule in a module sheet: `.ltable th`, `.dow-table th` and `.debt-main th` all set text-align at (0,1,1) and outrank the shared (0,1,0), so a module whose headers need to stay right-aligned restates it as `.<scope> th.hub-num`.
blueprints.why: Four tables in two modules had each written this cell and no two of the four rules matched. Trips asked for lining figures through font-variant-numeric, the stocks watchlist asked for the same thing through --feat-tnum, and the debt and weekly tables asked for tabular alone and got lining by luck of the face they inherit. Nothing any of them paints is a fact about a trip or a credit card: a column of numbers wants its digits to line up, everywhere.

blueprints.name: Stat
blueprints.purpose: A figure with a short label beside it in the flow: a column of the two, optionally boxed, and a grid that lays boxed ones out as separate tiles.
blueprints.use_when: Any headline figure a page wants read at a glance: a score, a total, a day's count, a weather reading. hub-stat alone for an unboxed stack, add hub-stat--tile for a boxed one, and put several tiles in hub-stat-grid when there are more than fit on a line.
blueprints.dont: Do not set the value's size or face here, and do not look for a shared label: every consumer reads its figures at its own size and in its own face, and its labels at its own tracking and colour, so the module sets all of that on its own class beside these. A module sheet that loads before components.css and needs to change a declaration hub-stat-v sets (trips' day summary adds lining figures) must scope up as `.hub-stat-v.<own>`, because a bare module rule at (0,1,0) loses on order. Do not put a tile with its own border colour or fixed radius on hub-stat--tile to get the box; finances' debt tiles keep their softer 4px rule and take only hub-stat-v.
blueprints.why: Trips built this five times, finances once and jobs once, and nothing any of them paints is a fact about a trip, a card or a company: a number worth reading at a glance wants the foreground colour and tabular figures everywhere, an unboxed stack wants the same 2px between figure and label, and a boxed one wants the card rule. That core is all they agreed on; the triage's single tile was an overread.

blueprints.name: Stat row
blueprints.purpose: A line of stats, centred on each other and wrapping onto a second line when the pane is narrow.
blueprints.use_when: Three or four stats that belong together in a detail pane: a blended score and the parts it is blended from.
blueprints.dont: Do not give the row its padding or divider here; where the row sits in a pane is the pane's call, and trips' detail panel draws it as a dashed-rule strip in one place and a card in another. For more than a line's worth of boxed stats, use hub-stat-grid instead.
blueprints.why: The row is the arrangement the stat tiles sit in, and it carries nothing about what is being scored.

blueprints.name: Track and bar
blueprints.purpose: A length read against a full width. The track is a clipped pill and is the scale; each bar inside it is a solid accent fill whose width is the amount.
blueprints.use_when: A figure worth comparing by eye across rows: a cost category against the largest one, a week's pay against the peak week, a score out of ten. Several bars in one track sit end to end, so a committed part and an open part can share one scale.
blueprints.dont: Do not set the length here; the module sets width (or a scaleX, as finances does so its slider does not re-lay out five rows). Height and ground are trips' defaults, not a rule: finances' 5px bar on the rule colour and jobs' 6px bordered one restate them as `.hub-track.<own>`, because both sheets load before components.css and a bare override loses on order. That includes a phone rule that hides the track: finances' `display:none` had to scope up too. A state colour (trips' hatched still-open segment, jobs' transparent empty fill) stays with the module.
blueprints.why: Trips, finances and jobs each drew this bar, and nothing it paints is a fact about a trip, a paycheck or a job: an amount against a scale is a shape. The three agreed on the clipped pill and the accent fill and disagreed on height, ground and border, which is how heavy a page wants its bars to read, so only the shape moved.

blueprints.name: Page shell
blueprints.purpose: The frame a module page sits in: a grid exactly one viewport tall, so the top bar and the status strip stay pinned and only the middle row scrolls.
blueprints.use_when: The outermost wrapper of any module page that has a top bar, a body, and usually a status strip. Put it on the div that holds those rows, beside the module's own shell class, which carries the rows.
blueprints.dont: Do not put rows here; the module owns them (trips and home stack a strip under the top bar, food and recipes have no status row, work and jobs have three). The phone release, where the frame lets go and the page scrolls as a document, stays module-side too, because the breakpoint differs per page. Pages whose sheet loads before components.css (finances, jobs, purchases) scope that release as `.hub-shell.<own>`, or the shared 100vh wins on order and the phone page is clipped to one screen. Trips releases through .hub-t3p in the tabbed-3-pane origin sheet, which loads after components.css. The same goes for a `100dvh` height on those pages. Checklists and stocks are flex columns and ledger's shell is unstyled; they are not this part.
blueprints.why: Nine pages drew the same frame, and a pinned top bar over one scroll region is a fact about a dashboard, not about trips, jobs or a recipe. They agreed on the grid and the one-viewport height and disagreed on everything below that, so only those two declarations moved.

blueprints.name: Field
blueprints.purpose: A label over its control, with an optional italic hint under it saying what an empty one means. Fields that share a line split it evenly, and a long form breaks into labelled sections, the optional ones folded behind a heading that shows + or minus.
blueprints.use_when: Any form in a dialog or a side panel: a new application, a booking, a candidate. Reach for the section heading once a form passes about ten fields, and for the folding group when a section only matters some of the time (what you know once a stay is booked).
blueprints.dont: Do not style the input, select or textarea through this part. Trips, jobs and purchases disagree on the control's padding, size, ground and focus ring, and a shared `.hub-field input:not(...)` rule would outrank jobs' single-class `.field-input`. A shared input shape is a later family of its own. The hint's size is the module's (trips 11px on a 1.5 line, jobs 12px). Jobs spaces its field 5px, and says so as `.hub-field.field` because its sheet loads before components.css. Trips keeps `field` beside `hub-field` because its label and control rules and its modal spacing still key on it.
blueprints.why: Trips, jobs and purchases each built the same label-over-control column, and trips and purchases to the pixel. A label over an input is a fact about a form, not about a stay, an application or a purchase. The italic faint hint and the section heading are how any long form stays readable, so those moved with it; everything about the control itself did not agree and stayed.

blueprints.name: Picker grid
blueprints.purpose: A set of options you tick, laid out as a grid of full-width hit targets. A picked option is tinted with the accent, and bulk actions (everyone, clear) sit on the label line.
blueprints.use_when: Choosing several of a known, short list: who a cost splits between, which people a thing is for. Put the grid inside a `hub-field`, with the head holding the label and the bulk actions.
blueprints.dont: Do not use it for a single choice (that is a select) or for a list long enough to need search. A lone `<i>` inside the grid is its empty line and spans every column. What the picked set means, and what an empty one defaults to, belongs in a `hub-field-hint` and in the module.
blueprints.why: Only trips' crew split draws it today, but nothing in it is about a crew: a tick list that reads as one control instead of loose checkboxes is a form part. It is promoted with the field it lives in so the next module picking several of anything starts from it.

blueprints.name: List row
blueprints.purpose: One item in a pickable list: a title and a sub line on the left, a figure or status on the right, and a 2px left edge that lights with the accent when the row is the one open beside the list.
blueprints.use_when: A rail or column of items where clicking one opens its detail: activities on a trip, applications in the jobs funnel. Put `selected` on the open row.
blueprints.dont: Do not set type or padding here; jobs sets its company in the body face at 16px and trips its place at 15px, and each module pads and rules its rows its own way. A status colour on the edge (trips' decided and matched rows) is the module's, scoped up past `.hub-row.selected` because that rule loads after the module sheet; so is a phone release that lets the title wrap (`.hub-row-title.<own>`) or restacks the right column (`.hub-row-right.<own>`). Jobs stacks its right column the same way. A table row is not this part; that is the table family.
blueprints.why: Trips' activity list and jobs' application funnel drew the same row, hover and selected state byte for byte. A title-and-figure row with a lit edge for the open item is how any master-detail list reads, not a fact about trips or jobs. They disagreed on type, padding and the right column's direction, so only the shape, the states and the one-line cut moved.

blueprints.name: Section nav rail
blueprints.purpose: A page's primary section switch set as a column of full-height entries: a flush 4px spine on the left, carded on the right, an uppercase label, and an optional quieter child list hung off one entry by a hairline.
blueprints.use_when: The leftmost column of a multi-section page, where which section you are in has to survive a glance: the trips board's sections and days, the /food area view's places, city and areas switch. Put `active` on the open entry and on the open child.
blueprints.dont: Do not set what the active entry's ground is here; trips fills it with an accent mix (and tunes that per vesper surface), food leaves it elevated. The label/glyph line, the count and a child row's cells are the module's. Pages whose sheet loads before components.css scope a phone release as `.hub-nav-item.<own>`, `.hub-nav-label.<own>`, `.hub-nav-subrail.<own>` and `.hub-nav-subitem.<own>`, and scope their active ground as `.hub-nav-item.<own>.active`, or the shared hover repaints the active entry. The top-of-page tab strip is not this part; that is the tab family.
blueprints.why: Trips' section rail and the /food area view's switch were the same rail built twice, down to the padding, the spine and the hover. A loud vertical section switch with an indented child list is how any multi-section page leads, not a fact about trips or food. They disagreed on the active ground and the line's alignment, so only the shape, the spine and the states moved.

blueprints.name: Checklist
blueprints.purpose: A bare list of things to tick, and the done state: once the item's checkbox is ticked its sentence dims and is struck through, the box itself untouched.

blueprints.name: Timeline
blueprints.purpose: A proportional hour grid: one column per day on a midnight-to-midnight axis, an hour gutter on the left, day heads on top, and a live current-time marker. `--tl-h` is the whole axis height and `--tl-days` (set inline) the column count. `is-today` colours a head, `is-mid` strengthens the midnight label, `strong` darkens a gridline. A `hub-timeline-block` is a timed item: its `top` is the start and its height the duration, with a time line, a name and a sub line; `selected` and `is-open` (no end time: a dashed, fading bottom edge) are its states. A `hub-timeline-inst` is an instant, a timed item with no duration (a departure, a check-in): a 2px rule at its exact minute plus a `hub-timeline-inst-l` label on its own line (`<i>` time, `<span>` name, `<em>` a qualifier that stays on the line), both `selected`-able; the module sets the label's `top`, and `--tl-inst` tints a kind. Grid row two is the untimed tray: an `anytime` label in the gutter and one `hub-timeline-tray` per day, holding a `hub-timeline-chip` (a name and an `<i>` sub line) for each item with no time, or `hub-timeline-tray-none` when the day has none; `selected` is the chip's state. On a phone it becomes a viewport-tall box that scrolls both ways with the heads and gutter pinned.
blueprints.use_when: Timed things where duration and gaps matter, laid on a real clock: an itinerary, a shift plan, a booking calendar. Put the positioned items inside `.hub-timeline-col` with a percentage `top` and height.
blueprints.dont: Do not confuse it with `hub-timeline-row` (a time beside an event, read as a list). Do not put a timed item in the tray: "no time set" is not midnight, and a time belongs on the axis. Do not give an item in a column a z-index above 5, or it prints through the pinned heads on a phone. To drop the internal scroller (a single-day view that scrolls with the page), scope it as trips' `.dayv` does: height auto, body overflow visible, gutter static, heads and corner hidden. The block's, the chip's and the instant's hover, `selected` and `is-open` states are zero-specificity (`:where()`), so a module's two-class kind rule (trips' `.hub-timeline-block.tl-flight`, `.hub-timeline-chip.tl-back`) wins over them in either load order; do not raise them. Kinds are module facts: dress the block or chip with a second class, never a new `hub-` modifier. Do not draw an item with no duration as a short block: a 30px box cannot hold a time, a name and a place, so it is an instant. Tint an instant kind through `--tl-inst`, never `--i`, which `selected` owns.
blueprints.why: Trips' itinerary drew this axis in trips.css, and none of its declarations names a trip: a day column, an hour gutter, a sticky head, a now line, an untimed tray and an instant mark are the shape of any timed plan. Home's `tb-day-*` hour grid is a separate React page that the stage 2 spec keeps out of scope, so it was not repointed.

blueprints.name: Pill
blueprints.purpose: A hairline pill that carries a reading: a badge on a board row, a verdict on a preference. It sets the shape and the tone (`is-good`, `is-warn`, `is-alert`) and nothing else. `hub-pill--dashed` is a reading not in yet, quieter and dashed. `hub-pill--filled` is the one pill in a row that must be planned around, drawn solid in the accent. `hub-pill-x` is the bare x button inside a pill that clears what the pill names (a search filter), drawn in the pill's colour.
blueprints.use_when: A short word or count whose colour is the message. Give it its own size in the module, next to the type it sits in. Dash a pill whose answer is still loading or missing, in the same slot the answer will take, so nothing moves when it lands. Fill at most the few pills a reader plans around; a row of filled pills shouts as loudly as none.
blueprints.dont: Do not add a size here or a fourth tone: every pill matches a different line of type, and three tones is the whole vocabulary. The dash and the fill are weights, not tones: do not combine either with `is-*` or with each other. The dash clears the background, which beats a module ground only where components.css loads after the module sheet (trips' board); elsewhere compound the ground as `.<own>:not(.hub-pill--dashed)`. A module shade between the base and the fill (trips' `want`) is compounded as `.cpill.cpill-want` so it beats `.hub-pill` in either load order. A module state that quiets a pill (trips' ruled-out row) needs more specificity than `.hub-pill.is-good`, which is (0,2,0). A `hub-tag` is a selectable filter, not a reading; do not swap one for the other.
blueprints.why: Trips' housing, flight and rental badges, the crew preference verdicts, the crew card's rating pills, the leave-by pill, the payer and split chips, and the activity status and tag chips each re-authored the same border, radius and three tone pairs, and none of those declarations names a trip. The sizes differ on purpose and stay with each module.

blueprints.name: Split pane
blueprints.purpose: A section's working area: a list column beside a detail column, laid out as a grid that fills what its flex parent leaves (`flex: 1`). The default gives the list two thirds and floors the detail at 320px. `hub-pane-col` is the list side: a flex column with a 0 floor that owns its own scroller and draws the divider on its right. Under 900px the two stack, list first, and the divider moves under the list. Inside the list column, `hub-pane-head` is the section's head (title, filters, the add button): a padded flex column that keeps its height and rules itself off, and `hub-pane-list` under it takes the rest of the column and scrolls. On the detail side, `hub-detail-rail` is the selected record's column: it takes what its parent leaves and scrolls on its own, and `hub-detail-rail-inner` inside it is the flex column the detail cards stack in. Under 900px a rail that also carries `hub-slide-over` is a phone sheet: hidden until the module adds `is-open` (when a row is selected), then fixed over the whole viewport at z 90 with its `hub-slide-over-close` back button showing on top, its inner stack scrolling, and the page behind it locked. The back button is hidden at every other width.
blueprints.use_when: Any three-pane module's middle and right columns: a list of records and the one that is selected. The section header sits above the split, not inside it.
blueprints.dont: Do not set the ratio on `.hub-split` itself from a module sheet: key it on a module attribute or class at two-class specificity (trips' `.focus-split[data-split="crew"]`), so it wins in either load order. A module that also puts a flex class on the same element (food's `.col`) must restate `display: grid` in its own sheet when that sheet loads after components.css. A module rule that changes `hub-pane-col`'s overflow or border must be two classes (trips' `.hub-pane-col.focus-col`): components.css loads after trips.css on the board. The empty line inside a pane is `hub-empty-state`, not a split part. Same for the head's phone padding (trips' `.hub-pane-head.focus-head`). Do not add a second scroller around content that scrolls itself: release the list with a two-class rule (trips' `.focus-list:has(.hub-timeline)`). Keep a module class beside `hub-detail-rail` for the module's own detail rules (trips' `.context .fdetail-head`), and write any override of its flex or overflow at two classes or more (trips' `body[data-tab="food"] .context`). A module map beside the rail must hide itself while the slide-over is open (trips' `.side-pane:has(.hub-slide-over.is-open) .side-map`): Leaflet's panes run to z 800 in the same stacking context. The launcher overlay is chrome, not this: theme-switch.js injects its own on pages that never load components.css.
blueprints.why: Trips and /food each built the same list-and-detail grid with only the ratio differing, and the blueprints layouts tab borrows it for its mockups. A list beside the selected record is the shape of any three-pane module; the ratio is the module's.

blueprints.name: Detail panel
blueprints.purpose: The selected record read out. `hub-detail` is a flex column; `hub-detail-head` is its first row, a padded flex line ruled off underneath with the title block on the left and `hub-detail-actions` (the record's buttons, which never shrink) on the right. `hub-detail-title` is the record's name in display type at 28px. `hub-meta-strip` sits under the head: a wrapping row of short facts, each a span whose `b` is the label (an icon or a word), ruled off with a dashed line. `hub-detail-body` is the rest of the record: a grid of `hub-detail-body-main` (the reading column, a stack of blocks) and `hub-detail-body-side` (240px of controls), split by a dashed rule. Each block in the body is a plain div: `hub-block-label` (10px caps) over its content, and `hub-block-text` for a paragraph, which keeps the record's line breaks. `hub-kv-row` is one stated fact inside a block: a `span` label on the left and the value in `b` on the right, spread across the row. `hub-link-row` is the pressable version of a kv row: a bordered `a` with `hub-link-row-t` (the label, which wraps), an optional `hub-link-row-v` value and a `hub-link-row-x` outbound mark. `hub-link-row--flat` on a `div` is a row with no destination, dashed and inert. `hub-callout-warn` closes a block with something to fix: a warn-edged line with the figure in `b`. `hub-detail-card` is one read in a rail (a summary, a total, a list of facts) on the card ground, headed by `hub-detail-card-head` in 10px caps; kv rows, link rows and callouts go inside it.
blueprints.use_when: The detail side of a list-and-detail module, when one record is selected and can be edited or deleted from there.
blueprints.dont: Do not put section filters or an add button in this head: that is `hub-pane-head`, above the list. A narrow rail tightens the head and title with a rule at two classes or more (trips' `.context .fdetail-head`, `.context .fdetail-title`), because components.css loads after trips.css on the board. Keep the module class beside each hub class for those rules. Keep `hub-meta-strip` to short facts; a paragraph belongs in a block below it. A narrow rail stacks the body with its own two-class rule (trips' `.context .fbody`); do not give `hub-detail-body` a responsive switch of its own. A rail that restyles the label (trips' `.context .fblk-l`) keeps the module class beside `hub-block-label`. Row states (a highlighted own row, a marked row) belong to the module and must compound on its class (trips' `.ctx-row.ctx-row-you`), or components.css wins them back on the board. Never put `hub-link-row--flat` on a link: a row that goes somewhere is pressable, and one that doesn't must not look it. `hub-callout-warn` is for a gap the reader can close, not for a failure: an error needs its own treatment. Do not nest a `hub-detail-card` in another, and do not use it for the list's cards on the board: those are `hub-card`.
blueprints.why: Trips renders the same head for activities, logistics rows, crew and expenses: a title and its edit and delete buttons. Nothing in it is about a trip, and any module that edits one record at a time needs the same head.

blueprints.name: Carousel
blueprints.purpose: A strip of photos you drag or flick through. `hub-carousel` is the frame: inset from its panel with its own hairline and radius, clipping what it holds. `hub-carousel-track` inside it is a native horizontal scroller with proximity scroll-snap, no scrollbar, a grab cursor and a mask that fades slides out across its 12px padding. Each `hub-carousel-slide` is a figure at its image's natural width and a fixed height (190 to 340px, 170 to 260px under 900px), snapping to the centre, with an optional `figcaption` laid over the bottom of the image. `hub-carousel-nav` (with `is-prev` or `is-next`) is a round smoked-glass arrow over the middle edge that shows only while the frame is hovered or the arrow has keyboard focus, `hub-carousel-count` is the matching readout in the bottom right, and `hub-carousel-credit` the matching link in the bottom left. The module sets `is-drag` on the track while a mouse drags it, and `at-start` or `at-end` when there is nothing further that way, which hides that arrow.
blueprints.use_when: A record has a set of photos worth looking through in place: a stay, a venue, a listing. Two or three slides show at once, so the next one's edge tells the reader there are more.
blueprints.dont: Do not give the slides a fixed width or aspect ratio: a portrait photo stays portrait and the strip reads as a filmstrip. Do not use mandatory snap: it turns every flick into a page turn. The track's drag, throw and the counter are the module's script (trips' bindShots and SPIN), not this stylesheet, and keep the arrows as the fallback input, never the only one. Do not drop the credit where the photo provider requires one.
blueprints.why: Trips draws it for a stay's photos, and nothing in it is about a stay: the frame, the snap strip, the hidden arrows and the glass readouts are how any module would show a set of photos without a lightbox.

blueprints.name: Fact grid
blueprints.purpose: Label and value pairs laid out to scan for one answer. `hub-fact-grid` is an auto-fit grid of columns at least 210px wide. Each `hub-fact` is a column pair: `hub-fact-k`, the label, in 10px caps at 500 weight on the muted colour, over `hub-fact-v`, the value, at 14px and 600 with tabular figures so clocks, codes and money line up, wrapping anywhere rather than overflowing. `hub-fact--wide` spans the whole row with a hairline and padding above it, for a value that is a sentence. `stay-fv--prose` drops a sentence-like value (address, host, parking) to 500 so the codes and names around it stay the bold ones.
blueprints.use_when: A booked or settled record read back as facts: confirmation codes, times, addresses, hosts, policies. Anything a reader jumps into for one value.
blueprints.dont: Do not render a blank value as a dash: drop the pair, or show `hub-pending`. Do not dim the label: a dimmed 10px cap runs under 4.5:1. Do not use it for prose or for lists; those go below the grid. A module rule that restyles something inside a value keys on its own class beside `hub-fact-v` (trips keeps `stay-fv` for its address chip).
blueprints.why: Trips reads a booked stay, flight and car back through it, and nothing in it is about travel: a record's facts as label and value, with sentences given their own row, is how any module shows a settled record.

blueprints.use_when: A settled record with fields nobody has filled in: the blank is ambiguous (unread and genuinely none look the same), so the line says which. Use the add button only when the reader can fill that field from here.

A module rule that sizes the button (trips' phone touch target) keys on its own class beside `hub-pending-add`.

blueprints.name: Column list
blueprints.purpose: Short factual lines, one per line. `hub-col-list` is an unmarked flex column of 13px lines at 500 weight on the muted colour. A keyed line is `hub-col-list-k` (dim, followed by a colon) then `hub-col-list-v` (full text colour). `hub-col-list-sub` is a line's own detail, set as an 11px block under it. `hub-col-list--two` flows the list into two columns of at least 260px with a small dot before each line, and `hub-col-list--steps` numbers the lines instead. `hub-col-groups` flows named groups into up to three columns of at least 240px; each `hub-col-group` stays whole, headed by `hub-col-group-k` in 10px caps (11.5px under 900px) ruled off underneath, and a group with the `hidden` attribute is gone.
blueprints.use_when: A record's lists: rules, notes, chores, amenities, fare conditions. `--two` for a flat list long enough to push what follows off screen, `--steps` for a sequence done in order, the groups for a long list that arrives already sectioned.
blueprints.dont: Do not use it for label and value facts you scan for one answer: that is `hub-fact-grid`. Do not set a fixed key width: the lists sit in cards of different widths and a ragged key edge beats a truncated one. Do not hide a line's detail behind a hover. For a checklist with ticks flowed into columns, use `hub-column-list`.
blueprints.why: Trips renders a stay's rules, chores, notes and amenity groups and a car's notes with it, and nothing in it is about travel: a record's short lists, keyed or not, bulleted or numbered or grouped, is how any module shows the lists a record carries.

blueprints.name: Chip toggle
blueprints.purpose: An on/off setting drawn as a pill around its own native checkbox. Hover lifts it; checked outlines it in the accent on an accent wash; keyboard focus rings it. The checkbox stays visible, styled, because it is what the keyboard and screen reader operate.
blueprints.use_when: A single setting that changes what the page shows next to it, where the reader should see its state at a glance: one car for everyone, include the optional stops.
blueprints.dont: Do not use it for picking one of several filters (that is `hub-tag` with `is-on`) or for a checklist row (that is `hub-checklist-item`). Do not hide the checkbox inside it: the pill is the checkbox's frame, not a replacement. The hidden attribute works on it because the component restates it.
blueprints.why: Trips' day-of ride card sets its one-car chain with it, and a visible on/off setting beside the thing it changes is a control any module can need.

blueprints.name: QR sheet
blueprints.purpose: A code to hold a phone out to. The sheet centres its svg at the width it is given, up to a size that still fits a phone in portrait with the facts under it in view, because a code you scroll to is a code nobody scans. The facts stack centred under it, one per line, in plain type for the camera that will not scan and the person who would rather type.

blueprints.why: Trips' stay dialog shows the wifi network as a QR so a guest's camera joins it, and any module that hands a value to another phone wants the same sheet.

blueprints.name: Chart
